app/src/lib/data.js:176 — home page derives sprite as front_default ?? spriteUrl(id), a different rule for the same concept

app/src/lib/util.js — pure shared helpers, no imports of app internals
app/src/components/Section.jsx, app/src/components/Card.jsx — components take plain props, no context or global state

coupling.rationale: Loose coupling with one clear data seam and idiomatic server/client separation; the dings are cosmetic (duplicated badge-link markup) and the untyped card contract, which is a deliberate JS choice but still an implicit interface.

evidence: app/src/lib/data.js:90-118 — cardsFromPokemonRefs correctly captures the real variation (alternate forms, dedupe, dex order) and is reused by three queries
app/src/lib/data.js:104,107 — its extra(ref) extension point is never passed by any caller (365, 390, 439)
app/src/lib/data.js:396-402 — the ability hidden flag bypasses that seam with a post-call mutation loop
app/src/components/Section.jsx:5 — Section supports an anchor prop, yet routes/pokemon/[name].jsx:104 re-implements the moves section by hand
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].jsx:120-127, moves/[name].jsx:55-61, abilities/[name].jsx:35-41, types/[name].jsx:47-54 — the null-data/NotFound wrapper is copy-pasted across all four detail routes
abstraction_design.rationale: The loadTypes/cardsFromPokemonRefs helpers are genuinely designed around the app's variation, but the abstraction is marred by one dead-and-bypassed extension point and a copy-pasted route wrapper, so extending it means duplicating rather than stretching it.

findings.issue: The sprite rule for Pokémon cards is implemented differently here (constructed URL by id) than on the home page (front_default with fallback) and again for artwork, so a fix for a species/default-pokémon mismatch is not guaranteed to cover every card list.
findings.suggestion: Extract one spriteFor(pokemonRecordOrId) helper and have both card paths use it, so the rule lives in one place.

findings.issue: getAbilityPage attaches the hidden flag by mutating cards after cardsFromPokemonRefs returns, bypassing the extra(ref) seam that exists precisely for this purpose — and that seam is dead code no caller ever uses.
findings.suggestion: Either pass extra to cardsFromPokemonRefs here (the ref has is_hidden available) or delete the unused parameter; keeping both invites the next editor to guess wrong.

findings.issue: Table body cells are hand-written while the header is driven by the COLUMNS array, and the level column is special-cased twice (line 14 and line 53), so a column change is a two-place edit that can silently desync.
findings.suggestion: Render both header and body from the same column definitions (key, label, accessor), keeping the level column as one flagged entry.

findings.issue: The Moves section is written out manually instead of using the Section component, although Section already supports the anchor prop needed for the #moves jump.
findings.suggestion: Use <Section title="Moves" anchor="moves"> so all sections share one implementation.

findings.issue: The show-NotFound-when-null / content-wrapper pattern is duplicated verbatim across all four detail routes.
findings.suggestion: Factor a small <DetailPage data={data()}>{...}</DetailPage> wrapper (or use a route-level ErrorBoundary) so not-found handling changes once.

findings.issue: num() (em dash for missing values) is defined here and again in app/src/routes/moves/[name].jsx:15.
findings.suggestion: Move it next to EM_DASH in lib/util.js; it is the app's missing-value convention.

findings.issue: updateParams and pageHref both hand-roll URLSearchParams manipulation of the same four query keys, so adding a filter means touching both and remembering the page reset.
findings.suggestion: Extract a single query-string helper (get/patch/build-href) used by both the controls and pagination.

findings.issue: The type-badge link markup and class convention (type-badge type-<name>) is rebuilt by hand here instead of reusing TypeBadgeLink from Card.jsx (also duplicated at routes/types/index.jsx:22).
findings.suggestion: Import TypeBadgeLink everywhere; the badge rendering then changes in one component.

summary: A small, current-idiom SolidStart v2 app with excellent data-source centralization and clean presentational components, so most changes land in one well-commented module. The main editability risks are the three-way duplicated sprite rule, a dead extension seam in cardsFromPokemonRefs that its one real use bypasses, and a half-columnar move table. I'd approve after the sprite helper and the extra/ref cleanup, since both are cheap and prevent future double-fixes.

Route files for each resource are copy-adjust, not stretch.

scenarios.change: Change the API base URL and caching rules
scenarios.notes: apiBase() (:18-20), the in-memory promise cache in apiFetch (:23-29) and spriteUrl (:83-84) are the only places that know these facts; no URL, cache key or env read appears anywhere else. Trivial. One caveat to note while in there: the cache also caches fetch failures as a never-expiring null.
